newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Helvatia plans no moves on U.S. lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Helvatia plans no moves on U.S. lawsuit.

text.p: Swiss insurer Helvatia Patria Holding said it planned no moves for the moment over a huge U.S. lawsuit alleging European insurers, including its Viennese subsidiary, withheld policies taken out by Holocaust victims.

Helvatia Patria said it had no basis to act on because all records at subsidiary Der Anker Allgemeine Versicherung AG were destroyed during World War Two and because it had received no notification of the suit.
"We have not received any written information about the suit from the plaintiffs or the court. All we know about this matter is from the media," spokesman Martin Huser told Reuters.
"We don't know yet what out next step will be. Based on this situation, we will wait and see what develops," Huser said.
Anker has already said crucial records went up in smoke in 1945 when allied bombs destroyed its Vienna headquarters.

"We cannot find these records and we believe they were all burned," Huser said, adding there had been no requests for old policies from Holocaust survivors or their heirs since Helvatia took over majority ownership.
Helvatia Patria first took a minority stake in Der Anker in 1962 but only took a majority in the late 1980s and boosted its holding to 99.9 percent in 1993, he said said.

In the class action suit on behalf of more than 10,000 people, the Holocaust victims and their families allege that the insurers withheld, concealed or converted the cash value and proceeds of policies sold before 1946 worth billions of dollars.
The suit is aimed at seven Austrian, German, French and Italian insurance firms.
Anker was owned from 1923 until 1943 by Swiss Reinsurance Co (Swiss Re), Huser said.
In 1944 it was bought by German insurers Viktoria and Bayerische Rueck, then at the end of the war taken over by the Austrian state under a policy of nationalising German companies.
In 1962, Austria sold the company to Swiss insurers Helvetia, Schweizerische Immobiliar and Neue Rueckversicherung, he said.
